primary_citation.official_title_verbatim_from_chaptered_t: An act relating to the safety of design and construction of public school buildings, providing for regulation, inspection and supervision of the construction, reconstruction or alteration of or addition to public school buildings, and for the inspection of existing school buildings, defining the powers and duties of the State Division of Architecture in respect thereto, providing for the collection and disposition of fees, prescribing penalties for violation thereof and declaring the urgency of the act, to take effect immediately.
primary_citation.in_effect: immediately upon approval (urgency act under California Constitution Article IV § 1, 1933 version)
primary_citation.primary_source_text_location: origin/1933_Vol1_Chapters.pdf (Statutes of California 1933, printed pages 352–355; PDF pages 353–356)

author.name_disagreement_resolution_status: Multiple secondary sources resolve to 'Charles Donald Field' (formal) using 'C. Don Field' (of record). Primary-source confirmation against the original bill or chaptered law signature TBD.
author.term: elected 1932-11-08; this Act was passed during his first term as a freshman assemblyman
author.intent_note: Field's original intent was to legislate broadly for most building types, but he narrowed the bill to public school buildings specifically to ensure legislative passage and enforceability. This is itself a doctrine lesson — the trade-off between scope and passage is recorded here for downstream analysis.

triggering_event.epicenter_CGS: 3 miles south of Huntington Beach, approximately 8 miles deep
triggering_event.fault: Newport-Inglewood Fault (right-lateral strike-slip, 46 miles total length from Culver City to Newport Beach)

casualties.manner_of_death_observation: approximately two-thirds of deaths occurred as people ran out of buildings and were struck by falling debris (per California Geological Survey)

school_building_damage.wikipedia_secondary_figure: 230 school buildings destroyed or rendered unsafe
school_building_damage.california_geological_survey_state_figur: 70 schools destroyed and 120 schools damaged (~75% of schools in the area)

school_building_damage.operational_significance: The earthquake struck at 5:54 PM PST — after most schools had dismissed for the day. Had the earthquake occurred during school hours, the death toll among children would likely have been catastrophic. This near-miss is the proximate cause of the legislative urgency.

section_outline: Section 1 — Construction of schools: Vests Division of Architecture with police-power authority to supervise construction of new school buildings (and reconstruction/alteration if estimated cost exceeds $1,000); defines 'school building' to include elementary, secondary, and junior college buildings of state, county, city, and any school/junior college district.

Section 2 — Issuance of Architecture to approve plans: Requires Division of Architecture to pass on and approve or reject all plans; requires school authorities to submit plans before adoption; requires written approval before any construction contract may be let; establishes fee schedule (one-half of 1 percent for first $50,000; one-quarter percent for excess over $50,000; minimum fee in any case $50; full fee paid into State treasury Public School Building Fund).
Section 3 — Invalid contracts: No contract for construction without prior Division approval shall be valid, and no public moneys may be paid for non-conforming work.

Section 4 — Reports: Architect/structural engineer in charge, the inspector, and the contractor must each periodically file verified reports of personal knowledge that work and materials conform to approved plans.
Section 5 — Rules: Division of Architecture authorized to make all necessary rules and regulations to carry out the act.
Section 6 — Penalty: Violation of any provision, or any false statement in a verified report, is a felony.

Section 7 — Inspection: Division has full authority to inspect; school district must provide competent, adequate, and continuous inspection during construction by an inspector under the responsibility of the architect/structural engineer and acceptable to the Division.

Section 8 — Inspection of existing buildings: On request of school board or 10% of parents (certified by county superintendent), Division must examine and report on structural condition of any existing public school building, with expenses payable by district (waivable on State Superintendent's recommendation if district cannot afford).

Section 9 — Urgency: Declares urgency under California Constitution Article IV § 1; recites the southern California earthquake series, the loss of life and property, the seriously damaged school buildings, and the need for the act to take effect immediately so that replacement buildings will be properly constructed.

agency_currently.operational_outcome_per_agency_verbatim: Since the Field Act was enacted in 1933, DSA's review and approval have ensured that there has never been a major structural failure at a public California K–12 school or community college.
